title: Predicting In-Hospital Mortality in Pediatric Sepsis: Machine Learning Development and Multicenter Validation.
summary: Eight algorithms were evaluated for in-hospital mortality using predictors from the first 24 hours of pediatric ICU admission. XGBoost had AUC 0.821 (95% CI 0.751–0.892) and was externally assessed on the PIC pediatric and MIMIC-IV adult databases; the latter tests biological generalizability, not pediatric clinical deployment.
ai_technology: Eight machine-learning algorithms use first-24-hour ICU variables; SHAP interpretation and spline calibration were applied to the selected XGBoost model.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: The retrospective development cohort was from Chongqing Children’s Hospital. XGBoost achieved AUC 0.821 (95% CI 0.751–0.892); external assessment used the PIC pediatric database and adult MIMIC-IV data.
evidence.unknown: Development was retrospective at one hospital; the external MIMIC-IV cohort was adult and supports biological generalizability only. No prospective pediatric workflow or mortality benefit was tested.
evidence.ai_role: Eight machine-learning algorithms use first-24-hour ICU variables; SHAP interpretation and spline calibration were applied to the selected XGBoost model.
